rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every anchor in s23 resolves at `ed4ba1ec41`: `_sweep_lapsed_holds` (`reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:244`, bound as `sweep=` at `:1458`) passes no launcher, `sweep` binds `launch = launcher` (`reckon/crew/resumption.py:2177`) and calls `dispatch_awaiting_reviews` in its review pass (`:2424`, inside the cited 2413–2464), which is defined at `reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py:526`. The cited `_prepare_attempt_records` anchor resolves to its call site at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3438` (the definition is `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2150`); that is the boundary marker the worker needs, not a defect.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the gate population still reads "test files importing `reckon.crew.recovery_review_dispatch`" although the section now declares `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` as a write path.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the evidence note sits on the repo's durable `docs/evidence/fragments/a-dispatch-returns-without-its-worker/` path (the directory exists and holds the plan's other notes) and the per-step log is on the investigating run's own `logs/`, not in the temporary crew home.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the section names mechanisms by what they do and introduces no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags into any symbol, file or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated cause (the launch stops between the claim's registration and the attempt record) matches the cited record set, and I confirmed it on the kept run directory: `claim.json` reads `claim_registered_at` 2026-11-09T01:38:18Z, `discard.json` reads `discarded_at` 2026-11-09T01:40:22.882965+00:00 (124.9 s, so "124 seconds later" is exact), and `classification.json` records `attempt.json` and `worker.json` as `absent`, while `reckon/crew/promotion.py:discard` removes only the pointer, the claim and the worktree, so the absence of `attempt.json` is evidence the launch stopped before `_prepare_attempt_records` wrote it. The mechanism produces the done-when, and the caller is named: `dispatch_review_for_run` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2605`) reaches `_dispatch_composed_review`, which calls `dispatch(... launcher=launcher)`; with `launcher=None` that is the `_prepare_attempt_records` branch at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3438`. I also checked the second route: the first listed instance (`r-20261108T163518843254-plan-review-of-a-read-costs-what-changed`) is a plan review, composed through `plan_review.compose_owed_plan_reviews` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:4036`) rather than `dispatch_awaiting_reviews`, but that caller is also given `launcher=launch` from the same sweep, so it enters the same `dispatch()` window and the named reproduction reaches it.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable (name the step a sweep-launched review stops at, and repair it if it lies in scope); the repair is conditional on the investigation rather than a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s23's relationships are as it needs them; s23 declares no depends-on, and the work it builds on (§19, done) is already landed, so naming it a dependency would add nothing; the write path it gained (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py`) matches where the window it localises actually lies (`_publish_launch_claim` called at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2570`, `_prepare_attempt_records` called at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3438`, both inside `dispatch()`).
